academia.rationale: DFKI and Fraunhofer sit in Hightech Agenda roadmap processes and academic experts are standing invitees at Bundestag hearings on AI implementation.

civil_society.rationale: AlgorithmWatch and vzbv filed statements on the KI-MIG draft and at the Bundestag hearing of 23 March 2026, but vzbv noted the absence of institutional anchoring for civil society in the governance…

industry.rationale: Bitkom and the KI-Bundesverband participated in the KI-MIG Verbändebeteiligung and Bundestag hearings, and industry is a named partner in the Hightech Agenda roadmaps launched 20 May 2026.

international.rationale: Germany negotiates and implements the EU AI Act, participates in OECD.AI, GPAI and the G7 Hiroshima process, and contributes through DIN/DKE to European AI standardisation.

actions_taken.rationale: No AI Act enforcement decision has been published in Germany since BNetzA supervision began on 2 August 2026.

dedicated_authority.rationale: BNetzA holds an explicit statutory AI remit with a dedicated market surveillance chamber, KoKIVO and complaints portal, established only on 29 July 2026 with contested resourcing.

monitoring_practice.rationale: A citizen complaints portal is live and KI-MIG requires an annual activity report to the Bundestag, the first covering 2026 and due 31 March 2027; no audits published yet.

sanctions_framework.rationale: KI-MIG sets the national fine regime under Art. 99 AI Act, up to EUR 35m or 7% of global turnover for prohibited practices and graduated lower tiers.

formal_coordination.rationale: KI-MIG § 5 establishes the statutory Koordinierungs- und Kompetenzzentrum (KoKIVO) at BNetzA to align all competent authorities, operating only since July 2026.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: LG München I rulings (GEMA v OpenAI, 11 Nov 2025; GEMA v Suno, July 2026) and the BVerfG's 2023 automated-data-analysis judgment shape AI law, with appeals pending at OLG München.

regulator_plurality.rationale: KI-MIG names BNetzA as central market surveillance authority while BaFin, BSI, BfArM, BfDI, Landesmedienanstalten and Länder DPAs retain their own AI remits.

subnational_role.rationale: Länder data protection authorities and Landesmedienanstalten implement AI rules within federal/EU frameworks; Länder enact AI strategies but no binding AI regulation of their own.

binding_instruments.rationale: AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, KI-MIG (2026), BDSG/GDPR, MDR and sector rules enforced by BaFin, BSI and BfArM operate together.

economic_tools.rationale: KI-MIG mandates at least one national AI regulatory sandbox at BNetzA, alongside Hightech Agenda Deutschland KI roadmap funding, KI-Robotikbooster and AI gigafactory investment.

institutional_capacity.rationale: BNetzA hosts the KoKIVO coordination centre, an instruction-free AI market surveillance chamber and the KI-Service Desk, all operational only since 29 July 2026 with criticised lead time.

soft_law.rationale: DIN/DKE Normungsroadmap KI, BSI AI security guidance, DSK data-protection guidance and March 2025 federal guidelines for AI in public administration are published, while harmonised AI Act standards…

ai_specificity.rationale: KI-MIG is a dedicated AI implementation statute executing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, not adapted general law.

binding_force.rationale: KI-MIG (Act of 22 July 2026, BGBl. I Nr. 223) in force since 29 July 2026 alongside directly applicable AI Act (EU) 2024/1689.

implementation.rationale: Prohibitions, GPAI and Art. 50 transparency duties apply and BNetzA supervises since 2 Aug 2026, but Annex III high-risk duties were deferred to 2 Dec 2027 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

scope.rationale: AI Act plus KI-MIG cover AI horizontally across all sectors, with sectoral supervision allocated to BaFin, BSI, BfArM and Landesmedienanstalten.
